text: Every single measure and every relationship you've built across the last five chapters lives inside what the service now calls a semantic model — the modern name for what used to simply be called a dataset, back before Microsoft renamed it.

There are three distinct ways a semantic model actually gets its data. Import copies the data directly into the model and stores it in memory for real speed, but it needs a scheduled or on-demand refresh to stay current with the source. DirectQuery queries the original source live, every single time, keeping it always current at the real cost of query speed. And Composite mixes both approaches together in one single model, Import for some tables and DirectQuery for others, wherever each one genuinely fits best.

Sometimes an organization's model already lives entirely outside Power BI, hosted in SQL Server Analysis Services or Azure Analysis Services instead. A live connection passes every single query straight through to that externally hosted model, without copying or duplicating any of that existing investment.

Not every user who opens up a semantic model can actually edit it — ownership controls that directly, and if you're not the owner, you see it in a strictly read-only mode. Row-level security adds another real layer on top, restricting exactly which rows different users can see within that same shared model. Lesson 72 covers sharing access to all of this properly, in full detail.
